title: lazycop init writes portable paths when engine is inside the workspace

outcome: lazycop init always writes absolute paths to engine scripts, which break when the engine lives inside a workspace cloned on a different machine.

When the engine is inside the target workspace, lazycop init writes workspace-relative hook commands and a ${workspaceFolder}-based MCP arg; when outside, it keeps absolute paths; re-running init replaces any prior absolute paths with exactly one handler per event; uninstall removes both path forms.
forbid: do not touch packages/engine, packages/page, or docs/product
do not edit .bob/ by hand — the developer re-runs init afterwards
no new parallel *-v2 or *-enhanced files — edit existing install.ts and templates.ts only
HOOK_SCRIPT_SUFFIX must still match both absolute and relative hook commands for isOurs() detection

evidence: npm run typecheck and npm test both pass (159/159); install.ts portablePaths() emits relative hook command and ${workspaceFolder} MCP arg when engine is inside workspace; absolute paths used when outside; withoutOurHooks strips both forms so re-init leaves exactly 4 handlers; 4 new tests cover all scenarios

disposition: lazycop init now writes workspace-relative paths (hook command and ${workspaceFolder} MCP arg) when the engine is inside the target workspace; absolute paths retained for external engines; 4 new tests covering all specified cases added to packages/cli
